messages:
olivia: Quick check — seen a few client reports where the 429 `Retry-After` is smaller than our `X-Quota-Reset` header. Which should clients prefer? Also some clients expect per-route reset to be authoritative.

ethan: We intentionally intended `Retry-After` to be authoritative for backoff (seconds). `X-Quota-Reset` is an absolute epoch ts for internal tooling. But that's messy if clients interpret differently.

maya: +1 on clarifying. Can we convert X-Quota-Reset to a delta instead? I.e., `X-Quota-Reset-Seconds` to avoid clock skew.

sam: Quick context: per-route resets are sliding windows; X-Quota-Reset currently returns window end epoch. For account-level resets we set a different header `X-Account-Quota-Reset`.

olivia: Is there a compatibility plan? We can't break older SDKs that parse epoch.

ethan: Proposal: Keep existing `X-Quota-Reset` epoch but add `X-Quota-Reset-In` (seconds). SDKs can pick `Retry-After` first, then `X-Quota-Reset-In`, then epoch as fallback. Backcompat preserved.

maya: That sounds reasonable. Also need to document precedence: `Retry-After` > `X-Quota-Reset-In` > `X-Quota-Reset`.

sam: Edge case: bursts where per-route returns 0 remaining but account-level has headroom. We should include `X-Route-Remaining` and `X-Account-Remaining` so clients can decide to retry on a different route/endpoint.

olivia: Good point — add `X-Route-Remaining: 0` and `X-Account-Remaining: 200` example. Should we expose `X-Preferred-Fallback-Endpoint`? That might couple server decisions into clients.

ethan: I'd avoid giving fallback endpoints in headers. Better to have documentation + SDK guidance: if route remaining 0 but account remaining > 0, suggest clients retry at lower SLO model or different route programmatically.

maya: For the rollout: can we add `X-Quota-Reset-In` in a small deploy and monitor SDK errors? rate-limits-bot can annotate.

rate-limits-bot: deploy scheduled — rollout `add-x-quota-reset-in` to canary at 12:30 UTC; monitors: quota-errors, client-sdk-parse-errors.

olivia: Cool. One more: how do we signal "soft 429" vs "hard 429" (i.e., best-effort degrade vs strict deny)? We get customer asks to prefer softer failure modes.

ethan: Suggest `X-Rate-Limit-Mode: soft|hard`. Soft = server may accept after short backoff; hard = don't retry until reset.

sam: Implementation note: soft retries should still increment server-side usage — we must prevent retry storms. We'll cap soft retries to exponential backoff + jitter.

olivia: OK I'll file a small doc and a PR for the header additions and precedence rules. tagging @ethan @maya for review. Thanks.

ethan: pinged for review — will look this afternoon.

maya: Thanks — will grep SDKs for epoch parsing and add fallback. :thumbsup:
